hyde_original.raw_output:
Color Propagation reconstructs clipped highlights by borrowing color information from nearby, non-clipped pixels and propagating it into the clipped area. This can preserve plausible color in highlights where one or more channels have lost detail, rather than leaving them neutral or discolored.

Its main limitation is that reconstruction depends on suitable surrounding color information. Large uniformly clipped regions contain insufficient evidence, and propagation may introduce incorrect colors, artifacts, or bleeding from neighboring objects. It cannot recover genuine detail when all channels are completely clipped.
